item.title: Director for the Study of International Relations, Broadly Understood
item.description: The Wissenschaftszentrum Berlin für Sozialforschung (WZB Berlin Social Science Center) is one of the leading global research institutions in the field of social sciences. It unites the social sciences to address society’s biggest challenges. The WZB conducts world-class problem-oriented basic research in the social sciences and connects research and society by engaging with decision-makers in the public and private sectors, civil society and the general public. By bringing together scholars from all over the world with their various methodological and disciplinary backgrounds - including sociology, political science, economics, and law -, the WZB fosters a vibrant and stimulating research environment that promotes interdisciplinary collaboration. Research at the WZB is characterized by long-term projects based on multidisciplinary cooperation and transnational perspectives. The current cross-cutting research topics at the WZB are: Climate, Democracy, Digitalization, Education, Gender, Health, International Orders, Migration, and Work. The WZB is a publicly funded non-university research institute and a member of the Leibniz Association. The WZB seeks to establish a new research department and to fill a permanent full-time position of Director (f/m/x) for the study of international relations, broadly understood. We aim to appoint a world-class scholar in political science, sociology, or economics who will establish and lead a team to implement an ambitious research agenda focused on theory-driven empirical research on transformations of the international order and shifting power relations. Specializations might include conflict and war, international security, contestation and legitimacy of international institutions and norms, transnational politics, international political economy, and global governance challenges, such as climate change, migration, trade, or development. Applicants should be well-established within the international academic community, have a distinguished record of excellence, as evidenced by outstanding international publications and other scholarly activities, and should have a proven track record in the supervision of doctoral theses and career development of young researchers. They should be interested in communicating their research findings to the general public. The new research department should be able to cooperate with others in the WZB’s environment of interdisciplinary social science research. Applicants are expected to present their vision for a long-term social science research agenda in relation to other research units at the WZB. Ideally, the successful applicant will be appointed to a Joint Professorship (W3) at a German university. We value diversity and welcome all applications – irrespective of gender, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion, disability, age, or sexual orientation. The WZB expressly encourages women or persons with migration backgrounds to apply. Equally qualified applicants with disabilities will be given preference. German language skills are not required. Applications must be submitted by 20 September 2026 via the above ' Apply ' button, including in one PDF file the following items in English language: 1) a cover letter, 2) curriculum vitae, 3) list of publications, and 4) a brief statement on current and planned research. The invitations to job interviews are expected to be sent out in November, 2026. Job interviews will likely take place on December 9-10, 2026. All interviews will take place at the WZB in Berlin, Germany. The position will be filled at the earliest possible date. If you have any questions regarding the job opening, please contact the president of the WZB, Prof. Dr. h.c. Nicola Fuchs-Schündeln, Ph.D. via director.appointment@wzb.eu . For further details about the WZB, please visit our website at: www.wzb.eu .

item.title: Senior Researcher - Demos Digital
item.description: Demos is Britain’s leading cross-party think tank producing research and policies that have been adopted by successive governments for nearly 30 years. Movements, ideologies and governments have come and gone, yet in this moment of global democratic emergency, Demos’s work could not be more urgent or relevant. Demos’s dedicated digital research hub - Demos Digital - is a centre of excellence in digital policy and is home to the Resilient Information Ecosystems pillar and the thread of Trustworthy Technology which looks at how technology, from AI to social media, runs through all of our pillars. Our team’s recent work has covered AI chatbot ‘electoral hallucinations’ and political deepfakes, growing risks around new forms of digital foreign interference in the UK’s democracy, mapping AI–excerbated information crises, and the culminating challenges driving a fragmentation in the UK around information and social consensus. We are looking for a brilliant Senior Researcher with demonstrable experience and/or interest in tech and media policy to join our digital policy team. item.description: The Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner (OPCC) is seeking a Communications and Engagement Officer to help deliver clear communications, strengthen public engagement and support the work of the Police and Crime Commissioner across Hertfordshire. This varied role sits at the heart of local policing, crime prevention and community safety. The successful candidate will support the planning and delivery of communications activity, ensuring residents understand how their views influence policing and community safety priorities. Key responsibilities include developing and delivering communications campaigns, managing media relations, monitoring and responding to media enquiries, and building positive relationships with journalists. The role involves creating engaging content for a range of channels, including the OPCC website, newsletters, press releases, annual reports, case studies and social media platforms. A significant part of the role focuses on public engagement and consultation. The postholder will design surveys, analyse public feedback, interpret data and identify opportunities to improve engagement with residents and partners. They will also support public meetings by preparing briefings, coordinating logistics and liaising with Hertfordshire Constabulary and other stakeholders. The role includes managing public enquiries and casework, ensuring residents receive responsive and professional customer service. The successful candidate will be confident dealing with sensitive and complex issues, able to build strong relationships and manage competing priorities effectively. Applicants should have experience creating compelling communications content, excellent written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to translate complex information into clear and accessible messages. Strong IT skills, including proficiency in Microsoft Office applications such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint, are essential. The OPCC is looking for a highly organised, proactive and motivated individual who demonstrates integrity, commitment and perseverance in all aspects of their work. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who wants to make a tangible contribution to policing, public engagement and safer communities across Hertfordshire through high-quality communications and stakeholder engagement activities. item.description: We are seeking an exceptional advocate with a policy, legal or related digital rights campaigning background to work with us furthering privacy and civil liberties in the UK at one of the UK’s leading rights NGOs. The Senior Advocacy Officer will help us to lobby UK Parliament to further privacy and wider rights at a critical time – when a legal framework on police use of facial recognition is very soon to be introduced, and police are expanding their use of AI and new surveillance technologies. You’ll build on your strong experience to be a credible and proactive lobbyist in Parliament, write expert briefings and be confident meeting parliamentarians, take a leading role liaising with policy stakeholders, be a leading advocate in the press and the public forum, develop policy positions on key issues, and help drive our public campaigns for change. item.title: Assistant Professor in Danish Politics
item.description: The Department of Political Science and Public Management at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, invites applications for a 4-year Assistant Professorship in Danish Politics, commencing on 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. We are seeking a candidate with a strong research profile in Danish politics. Relevant research areas include, but are not limited to, political institutions, political parties, voter behaviour, gender and politics, public administration, lobbying and interest representation, public policy, political legitimacy, and democracy. Applicants may be specialists in Danish politics or comparativists whose research agenda includes Denmark as a major case. The position is open to all methodological approaches. What matters most is a strong commitment to conducting high-quality research and delivering excellent teaching in Danish politics. Application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST) See the entire call and apply by clicking the 'Apply' button
item.dc:creator: University of Southern Denmark

item.title: Constituency Assistant
item.description: Steff Aquarone, MP for North Norfolk, is seeking an organised, thoughtful and dependable Constituency Assistant to join his team permanently in North Walsham. This varied role combines responsibility for the MP’s diary and correspondence with practical support for constituent casework. The successful candidate will help ensure Steff’s time is well managed, commitments are properly planned and everyone contacting the office receives a prompt, compassionate and professional response. One moment may involve arranging meetings, visits or travel; the next may involve supporting a distressed resident, drafting a reply, logging a case or escalating an urgent enquiry. Key responsibilities: • Manage Steff’s diary, meetings, visits, travel and accommodation. • Prepare information and practical details for engagements. • Provide confidential administrative support and assist with surgeries and public events. • Oversee correspondence channels, including the MP inbox. • Triage enquiries and identify urgent, sensitive or safeguarding matters. • Respond clearly and compassionately by email, telephone and in person. • Log cases, gather information and monitor actions and deadlines. • Support the casework team while maintaining confidentiality and data protection. • Occasionally work outside normal hours or travel when required. The ideal candidate will be organised, reliable and attentive to detail. They will remain calm when priorities change, communicate clearly, exercise sound judgement and treat people with patience and dignity. They should be confident using email, digital calendars, case-management systems and shared documents, and able to identify what requires routine handling, specialist casework or Steff’s attention. Previous parliamentary experience is not essential. Relevant experience may come from public services, customer service, executive support or another demanding public-facing environment. Steff’s team is committed to compassion, integrity and high-quality public service. Applications are welcomed from all backgrounds, and reasonable adjustments will be made throughout recruitment and employment. The salary is £26,039 per annum, in accordance with IPSA guidelines. Appointment is subject to the Baseline Personnel Security Standard. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Closing time: 11.59pm First-round interviews: 26th August in North Walsham Second-round interviews: late August/early September Preferred start date: 1 October 2026 , subject to notice periods and security checks. We will not appoint before the closing date. Application Details Please email your CV and a covering letter of no more than 500 words to tom.garrod@parliament.uk , using the subject line “Constituency Assistant – [Your name]”. Please include examples of managing competing priorities and communicating sensitively with someone in difficult circumstances. Audio or video applications are welcome where this would remove an accessibility barrier. Applicants selected for interview will be contacted on 19 August 2026. We may not be able to contact unsuccessful applicants individually. Website : http://steffanaquarone.com/
item.dc:creator: Steff Aquarone MP (North Norfolk)

item.title: Communications Officer
item.description: Chris Murray is looking for a highly motivated, politically aware and organised individual to join his team. As a Communications Officer, you will play a key role in communicating Chris’ work to constituents across Edinburgh East and Musselburgh. Spanning traditional and new media, you will plan, coordinate, and deliver media and digital communications outputs of Chris’ work in Westminster and his constituency, communicating how his work impacts constituents. You will also identify opportunities to proactively communicate on local campaigns, and help secure impact and influence in the constituency. If you can think creatively and work flexibly as part of a small team, we would like to hear from you. To be successful you will have experience of working in a communications or media environment; knowledge of the local media would be great; but more importantly a keen interest and passion for the issues that matter a must. The ideal candidate would have: • Strong experience working in social media communications • Technical expertise in producing high quality content • Demonstratable experience in engaging different with varied demographic • Previous experience in a political office is not necessary but a grasp of how to shape public and political debate would be very helpful • Able to work independently and as part of a small, collaborative team • Excellent researcher skills with strong analytical and problem-solving skills Key responsibilities: • Develop targeted communications campaigns across a range of platforms • Monitor local, regional and national media coverage and identify issues of relevance • Monitor social media activity and provide insight on emerging trends and constituent concerns • Monitor and interpret legislation, parliamentary business, debates • Manage and produce a monthly newsletter using Mailchimp • Create, edit and publish engaging social media content • Draft external communications, press releases and public statements • Conduct detailed research and analysis on a wide range of policy and constituency issues Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates 14 August 2026 First interviews will be conducted by teams during the end of August, follwed by a second in-person interview. Flexible working will be considered. Application Details Please send your CV to ellis.milsom@parliament.uk with a cover letter of no more than 500 words. Website : https://www.chrismurraymp.com

item.title: Operations Manager
item.description: We are seeking an experienced, highly organised and proactive Operations Manager to play a central role in keeping our London office running smoothly and supporting our wider team and organisation. The ideal candidate will have strong liberal instincts and support our mission to defend civil liberties in the UK. This is a varied and hands-on role with responsibility across multiple operational areas, ensuring everything runs smoothly behind the scenes. It is a new role to the organisation, initially offered as a 12 month fixed term contract, with the possibility of extension. Flexible working that works for you 16 hours per work, with flexibility as to how these are worked We’re open to a range of working patterns (e.g. school hours, shorter days across the week, or compressed hours, potentially variations across term times / school holidays) Hybrid working, in practice will likely require min. 50% office attendance The rest of our team works full time in-office. However, for this particular part-time role we aim to agree on a working pattern that provides consistency and predictability while fitting around your other commitments. We particularly welcome applications from experienced candidates returning to work after a career break, including parents and carers. Operations Manager job description • Take ownership of the day-to-day running of the London office, ensuring it is organised and efficient • Help co-ordinate logistics for meetings and staff travel • Co-ordinate IT support, equipment and asset management • Lead IT migration projects (e.g. changing software/support suppliers, as directed) • Ensure the office and kitchen are adequately supplied • Support with HR admin including recruitment of staff, volunteers and contractors • Organise staff socials • Organise cycle to work scheme • Liaise with accountants, support basic book-keeping (receipt filing) • Support with internal file storage, physical and digital • Support with maintenance of databases • Assist with postage and physical mailouts to our supporters • Commit to highest standards of data protection • Periodically undertake required office risk assessments Closing Date : 21 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates ASAP Application Details First you must read the Job Information Pack on our website: https://bigbrotherwatch.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Operations-Manager-Job-Information-Pack-July-2026.pdf Then please send: • Your CV • A covering letter detailing how you meet the job specification, your relevant experience and why you want to work with Big Brother Watch in particular. (1 page maximum) To recruitment@bigbrotherwatch.org.uk ONLY applications sent directly to this email address will be considered. Website : https://bigbrotherwatch.org.uk

item.title: Senior Researcher
item.description: Key Information Hours: Full time (35hrs per week), Mon to Fri Location: Flexible working minimum 2 days per week in Shoreditch office Start Date: Immediate (notice periods will be taken into consideration) Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. About the Role BESA is seeking a Senior Researcher on an initial six-month fixed-term contract to help develop its in-house research capability. The role will lead a major study on social value in the procurement chain, covering research design, delivery, analysis and report writing. The successful candidate will also support the wider research programme, including managing external research partners and ensuring projects are delivered on time and to a high standard. This temporary role will help BESA assess the longer-term need for an in-house research function and strengthen the value of its research for members, policymakers, educators and system leaders. Key Responsibilities Conduct rigorous qualitative and quantitative research and analysis including: Carrying out literature reviews; Completing desk research and interviewing stakeholders in the education sector: e.g. policymakers, suppliers, system leaders. Contribute to the drafting of reports, briefings and related outputs. Represent BESA at external meetings, events and in the media. Lead and manage projects from conception to launch. Support the communication of our research through social media and other channels. Coordinate and quality assure quantitative research delivered by external partners and suppliers. Essential Experience Experience of conducting policy, market, social or applied research. Experience of qualitative research methods, including interviews, evidence synthesis or thematic analysis. Experience of drafting research reports, briefings or analytical outputs for non-specialist audiences. Experience using desk research to provide context, evidence and interpretation. Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, structured and accessible analysis. Ability to manage competing tasks and work to agreed milestones. Desirable Experience of education policy, procurement, public services, social value or supplier markets. Experience working in a membership body, trade association, think tank, research agency, consultancy or policy environment. Closing Date : 10 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates BESA will review applications as they are received. Early applications are encouraged, as suitable candidates may be invited to interview before the closing date. The start date for this role is immediate (notice periods will be considered) Application Details Please send your CV and a covering letter outlining your interest in the role and why you would like to work at BESA to Peter Doyle, Head of Policy & Research, peter@besa.org.uk Website : http://www.besa.org.uk/

The ideal candidate will be highly motivated and enthusiastic, with excellent writing skills and able to work autonomously. Responsibilities: • Research local, regional, or national issues to support the MP’s work and write briefings accordingly • Deal with complex queries on the MP’s behalf, including drafting letters, speech-writing, and responding to consultations • Maintain and utilise knowledge of relevant legislation, including impact on the local constituency • Keep up to date with parliamentary business, including debates, legislation, motions and Hansard. Ensure the MP is fully briefed questions and motions likely to be raised in Parliament. • Understand current and upcoming legislation and its impact on the constituency. • Diary management for days the MP is in Westminster • Arrange, attend and participate in meetings/events as appropriate • Provide general administrative support • Undertake casework • There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of normal working hours and/or travel Person Specification: • A can-do, dedicated and proactive approach • Self-motivated, well-organised and able work to very tight deadlines • Personable and able to communicate with people from all backgrounds • A high standard of written work • Excellent attention to detail • Ability to anticipate needs, take initiative, and resolve issues before they escalate • Sympathetic to the aims and values of the Labour Party Applicants with parliamentary experience are preferred. item.title: Caseworker
item.description: Uma Kumaran MP is recruiting a fixed term Caseworker to join her small and busy team. The role will include providing information, advice and support to constituents in Stratford and Bow on a variety of issues and liaising with both local councils, Government agencies, the voluntary sector and others to help resolve matters on behalf of constituents. Key responsibilities: Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as assisting on more complex cases from members of the public by phone, email, social media, or face-to-face. Ongoing communication may be required. Log all cases; monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken. Gather relevant information to assist with resolving cases. Draft responses to constituents. Assist surgeries and other meetings and follow up as appropriate. Ensure all enquiries are dealt with in a timely manner. Critically analyse patterns of enquiries and articulate the findings in reports and communication with the MP and other staff members. Manage and monitor casework enquiries received by social media. Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with the data protection legislation. There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for work occasionally. Personal specification: Previous experience of handling casework, either in an MP’s Office, the Civil Service, or a third sector organisation such as the CAB is desirable. Excellent verbal and written communication skills and confidence in interacting with people at all levels and in a variety of circumstances. A compassionate person with a strong sense of justice, a natural ability to empathise with others, and a determination to fight for fair outcomes. Ability to adapt and work effectively as part of a small team who manage diverse and varying workloads collaboratively. Ability to carry out tasks quickly and to a high standard. Being a self-starter with a demonstrable record of taking initiative. Ability to manage a large and varied caseload under pressure. An understanding of the values and aims of our team and the Member of Parliament. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 16 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews to be held w/c 24th August Application Details A written CV no longer than 2 sides of A4, along with a covering letter no longer than 1 side of A4. Please send via email with the subject line ‘Caseworker Application’ to my Head of Office at beatrice.morrison@parliament.uk. Website : https://www.umakumaran.co.uk/

item.title: Executive and Events Officer
item.description: We’re looking for a talented and motivated candidate to join our Communications, Partnerships and Events team as an Executive and Events Officer. This post offers a real opportunity to progress within our organisation. As an Executive and Events Officer at EPI, you will have the opportunity to: Broaden your skills in a fast-paced environment as part of our Communications, Partnerships and Events team; Support policy-relevant events that have a real impact on the ground; and Support and contribute to the growth of the organisation. About EPI The Education Policy Institute is an independent, impartial and evidence-based research institute that promotes high quality outcomes for all children and young people, regardless of background. We are known for producing research that both informs and influences public debate and policymaking. Responsibilities Support delivery of high-profile events, including our Annual Lecture, policy roundtables and party conference programme. Duties include drafting and sending invitations; communicating with speakers, delegates and event partners; compiling and circulating agendas; and managing venue logistics such as sourcing quotes and event set up. Support the communication of EPI’s events programme across all channels. Manage the diary of EPI’s CEO. Ensure day-to-day running of the office, including premises and facilities liaison, as well as supervising the EPI phone line. Working with the Finance Manager to support EPI’s financial operations, including managing invoicing processes and expenses, updating bookkeeping software and collating financial reports, supporting quarterly VAT return Organise Advisory Board meetings across our grant funded work. Organise and oversee our approach to recruitment; equalities and diversity monitoring; job postings and other organisation administration. Provide support to the governance of EPI – compiling trustee papers, arranging meetings and liaising with Trustees. This role will report to the Associate Director for Partnerships and Events. Please find more information about the role, including requirements and what we offer, here: https://epi.org.uk/jobs/executive-and-events-officer-july2026/ Closing Date : 17 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will take place w/c 24th August preferably in person, though we can be flexible for the right candidate. The interview will ask the questions about your skills and experience, and there will be several accompanying tasks to be completed beforehand. Application Details To apply, please fill out our application form ( https://www.smartsurvey.co.uk/s/HWZG8J/ ) with applications closing at 23:59. We are looking for someone to start by the end of September, and applications will be considered on a rolling basis. Website : https://epi.org.uk/

item.title: Research Executive / Associate Consultant
item.description: Lexington is a leading independent strategic consultancy. We are seeking an ambitious Research Executive (RE) or Associate Consultant (AC) to join our growing health practice in London. We welcome applications from candidates with some relevant experience (RE) / 1-2 years' experience (AC) in consultancy, communications, public affairs, policy or media within healthcare. Our team works with UK and global organisations across the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medtech, NHS and charity sectors. We help clients address major healthcare challenges, including access to innovative medicines and health inequalities. We deliver integrated communications, public affairs, policy and stakeholder engagement programmes, offering broad consulting experience and development opportunities. Key responsibilities Analyse developments across Government, Parliament, the NHS and the wider landscape Conduct research and generate insights to support client programmes and campaigns Draft high-quality materials including briefings, reports, stakeholder communications, press materials, social media content and presentations Assist with stakeholder engagement involving policymakers, NHS leaders, healthcare professionals, patient groups and industry stakeholders Support client events, advisory boards, parliamentary events, roundtables and healthcare congress activity Contribute to campaign development and content creation across multiple channels Contribute to new business activity, including research, proposals and pitches About you We are looking for candidates who can demonstrate: Some/1-2 years' relevant experience A strong interest in healthcare, the NHS, health policy and current affairs Excellent written and verbal communication skills Strong research, analytical and organisational skills The ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment Strong attention to detail and a willingness to learn A collaborative, proactive approach to problem-solving Experience in either public affairs and policy or communications and media relations is desirable, but applicants do not need experience across both disciplines. At Lexington, we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace and diverse workforce. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, ethnicity, religion, gender identity, sexual orientation or disability. item.title: Caseworker
item.description: Andy Slaughter MP is looking to recruit a highly motivated individual to join his busy constituency team as a Caseworker. As part of a team, the successful candidate will ensure that casework is progressed appropriately on behalf of the Member and will offer advice and support to constituents on a wide range of issues. The successful candidate will operate in a demanding political environment and must possess the ability and motivation to respond to a large and varied workload. Key Responsibilities Deal with daily enquiries from members of the public by phone, email, letter and in person ensuring that constituents are responded to in a manner which reflects the Member’s views. Gather relevant information in order to progress or close a constituent’s case through liaising with Government and local agencies. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of relevant guidelines/legislation as appropriate in dealing with casework. Log and monitor progress of all cases and ensure all records and information is stored confidentially, in line with GDPR and Data Protection guidelines. Assist with the work of other colleagues as required and communicate appropriately with internal and external contacts. Desirable Skills Experience working and dealing with the public is essential. Good IT skills including MS Office applications. Ability to manage a large and varied caseload under pressure, and carry out tasks quickly and to a high standard. Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills. An awareness of the functions of a Parliamentary office and a willingness to ‘muck in’ with the work of the office. Sympathetic to the aims and values of the Labour Party. Previous experience of casework or an advisory role, with an understanding of immigration, housing and benefit systems in the UK. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . item.title: Executive assistant
item.description: Lauder Teacher is a specialist strategic advisory firm operating at the intersection of real estate, infrastructure, technology and capital markets. We advise ambitious private companies, global investors and listed businesses on reputation, growth and influence. Our work spans strategic communications, investor relations, market intelligence, public affairs, executive profiling and broadcast media. We also co-produce one of the sector’s leading podcasts with Property Week. About the role This is a pivotal role at the heart of the business. Working directly with our founders and leadership team, you’ll help keep the business running smoothly while ensuring opportunities don’t get missed. You’ll combine strategic thinking with outstanding organisation, supporting business development, research, client projects and day-to-day operations. No two days are the same. You might coordinate meetings with FTSE CEOs, prepare briefing notes for podcasts, research potential clients, organise events, support major proposals or help solve operational challenges across the business. Key responsibilities Coordinate priorities for the founders and leadership team. Manage diaries, travel, meetings and schedules. Research clients, sectors and market trends. Support business development, proposals and pitches. Prepare briefing notes, presentations and background research. Help organise events, podcasts and client roundtables. Improve internal systems and ensure projects stay on track. If you’re looking for a traditional administrative role, this probably isn’t it. If you enjoy working at pace, taking ownership and being at the centre of a growing business, we’d love to hear from you. item.title: Political Assistant
item.description: Do you have political or local government experience? Are you confident dealing with the press, managing social media outlets and providing political advice to senior local politicians? Are you a member of the Reform Party or do you share the party's beliefs and values? Providing research, political advice and support to the Reform Group Leader and Reform councillors in Hull, you will draft and present reports, provide high quality support, plan agendas, attend and minute meetings and liaise with outside bodies and the press on behalf of the Reform Group. You will assist the group in its relationship with the local press and proactively ensure that the group's messages are developed and communicated widely, through a variety of media outlets. At the same time, you will ensure that key decisions from Group meetings are swiftly implemented and proactively identify issues of political interest, whilst supporting councillors with public speaking engagements and formal council questions and motions. You will be knowledgeable about the functions of a local authority and will be familiar with the roles of councillors and political party groups and will be able to work in a politically sensitive environment. Equally importantly, you will bring considerable initiative to support the Reform Group to undertake their role, and will display a very organised and self-motivated approach, backed by a high level of IT literacy and a sensitive approach to managing confidential information. Finally, you will need to be able to understand the diverse needs of the Reform Group and balance individual councillors' demands and expectations. As well as taking direction from the Leader of the Group you will work closely with the Group Whip and Democratic and Member Support colleagues. Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews will take place week commencing Monday 31 August 2026 Application Details https://hull.wd103.myworkdayjobs.com/en-GB/HCC/job/Political-Assistant_JR0000816 Website : https://www.hull.gov.uk/

item.title: Workplace and Inclusion Officer
item.description: The Workplace and Inclusion Officer will be the staff member responsible for the Board of Deputies’ work to ensure British Jews flourish in the workplace and in other parts of society including when accessing public services, especially health services and education. This includes combatting discrimination that may stem from antisemitism and promoting Jewish cultural competence. The post holder will be the staff lead on the Board of Deputies “BoD@Work” workstream, which includes supporting and developing Jewish Staff Networks, advocating for workplace best practices, and engaging with civil society, professional bodies, and Trade Unions to foster inclusive environments. The officer will also contribute to the goal of fostering inclusion within the Board and act as the Secretariate for the Under 35’s Assembly. The Officer will conduct this work in collaboration with the Boards’ wider Public Affairs Team and in support of the Boards’ Honorary Officers. item.title: Digital Content and Communications Officer
item.description: Lucy Rigby KC MP is looking for a creative, proactive and detail-oriented Digital Content and Communications Officer to suggest and create compelling and engaging content for audiences across digital channels. This role would suit someone who has very good creative and digital skills - most particularly in video. This is an exciting opportunity to join a dedicated team serving local people - supporting Lucy to be an active, impactful and approachable MP. This role will be 3 days a week and can be based either in Westminster or in Northampton. If the successful candidate is based primarily in Westminster, frequent travel to Northampton will be essential (likely at least once a week). Key Responsibilities: • Deliver end-to-end high quality, high engagement, video content to promote the MP’s’ work and campaigns across the constituency– including content ideation, and filming and editing short-form and long-form pieces tailored for a range of online channels • Accompany the MP to visits and events across the constituency, capturing and creating compelling content • Produce visual assets for social media using software such as Edits and Canva • Proactively lead on digital strategy, including planning, creating and developing engaging content across a wide range of channels • Edit and subtitle video clips using appropriate software • Produce a monthly digital newsletter • Manage the MPs’ website and monitor social media channels • Suggest content ideas, formats and trends to grow reach and engagement • From time to time, draft content for media, such as press releases, where relevant • Provide proactive communications support for local issue-based campaigns Essential Skills and Experience: • Strong skills and experience in digital content creation and delivery • Understanding of digital media trends • Ability to react quickly to news. • Strong organisational and time management abilities • Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and use initiative, with good attention to detail • Excellent written and verbal communication skills • Ability to translate policy into clear visual stories • There may be a requirement for the role holder to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for work occasionally Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). item.title: Campaigns Manager (South West)
item.description: Lead and deliver winning campaigns in priority areas across the regions, directly managing key contests where required and ensuring campaigns are professional, compliant and strategically focused. Work closely with MPs, candidates, councillors and local party teams to run structured campaign planning meetings, set clear objectives and drive progress against voter contact, fundraising and organisational targets. Build sustainable and self-sufficient campaign teams in held seats by strengthening volunteer recruitment, leadership capacity and local fundraising. Develop campaign-ready infrastructure in emerging priority seats, including clear strategy, messaging frameworks, data-led targeting and measurable growth plans. Support and develop local organisers and campaign staff through mentoring, training, and, where agreed, line management, helping to grow a confident and capable regional team. Embed best practice in data, digital campaigning, literature production and compliance across the region. Person specification We are looking for a strategic campaigner who understands what it takes to win competitive elections and can help others raise their game. What matters most is a track record of delivering results in high-pressure, target-driven campaigns. You will demonstrate: Experience in managing or playing a senior role in complex campaigns with measurable outcomes. A strong understanding of political messaging and how to translate strategy into compelling communications across print, digital and direct voter contact. The ability to analyse data and voter insight to inform targeting, messaging and resource allocation. Strong leadership skills, with experience motivating volunteers or staff, building effective teams and building positive relationships with stakeholders. Sound political judgement and an instinct for what resonates with voters. The confidence to challenge constructively, set high standards and hold teams accountable for delivery. The ability to work independently across a large region, prioritising effectively and responding calmly to unexpected developments. You will be someone who combines strategic thinking with practical delivery, and who enjoys working with teams at different stages of development — from well-established strongholds to emerging growth areas. Closing Date : 7 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Application Details Please fully read through the requirements of the job before applying, and take a few minutes to complete our Equality and Diversity Monitoring Forms, then proceed with your application. A full CV of no more than two pages, including a telephone number and email address A covering letter (no more than one A4 page) setting out why you want the job and how your experience and skills are relevant to it To be considered for this position, please submit your application to recruitment@libdems.org.uk. https://www.libdems.org.uk/work-for-us/federal-vacancy/campaigns-manager-south-west-1 Website : https://www.libdems.org.uk/

This is an excellent opportunity to join the office of an active constituency MP as Office Manager. The successful candidate will lead the administrative operation of a busy Parliamentary office, overseeing the office team, managing the budget and liaising with IPSA on financial and contractual matters. The successful candidate will have strong organisational and people-management skills, sound judgement, and the ability to manage a varied workload, including delegated signoff on relevant areas of office business, in a fast-paced environment. Lead and maintain a highly professional administrative support function for the MP’s office. Issues you can expect to work on include crime, local government matters, and immigration. item.title: PhD Studentship: Masters plus PHD- Sustainability Life Sciences
item.description: Scholarship Opportunity This is an opportunity to undertake a fully funded masters’ degree and an interdisciplinary PhD under the ‘Sustainable Transitions – Leverhulme Doctoral Training Programme’ at the University of Essex. (All tuition fees are covered and an annual stipend provided throughout the Masters and PhD phases.) The purpose of this programme is to train the next generation of interdisciplinary scholars with the skills and expertise to contribute to ‘sustainable transitions’ at local, national and international levels. Applicants with an undergraduate degree in the life sciences or a related subject are invited to put forward a proposal for a PhD research project in the field of environment and sustainability as it relates to the life sciences. The successful applicant will then undertake the following masters’ degrees commencing in January 2027 and further develop their research proposal before proceeding to the PhD phase: MSc Biotechnology Research Proposal You are invited to submit a 1000 word (max) project area proposal that describes the area that you wish to research. This call for proposals is broadly defined, leaving scope for the applicant to develop their own specific research proposal as part of the application. The successful candidate will further develop their proposal in close consultation with the supervisory team during the masters’ year and further during the PhD phase. In your proposal you should identify ONE of the following four disciplines that you would like to integrate into your research to ensure that it your research is interdisciplinary in nature: Law, Government/Political Science, Business, or Sociology. It is not necessary to have any prior knowledge of this additional discipline as you will be given training when you commence your PhD. Training and Support You will receive a range of training and opportunities in the Masters’ phase of the programme. When you commence the PhD phase you will receive support through the Sustainable Transitions training programme, which offers interdisciplinary research methods, secondary discipline training, and ongoing development. Doctoral scholars also have access to £2,500 through Proficio for training courses and £10,000 for research and additional training. You may audit relevant courses and will be supported by both the Sustainable Transitions management team and your supervisory team. Additionally, all scholars can join the University of Essex’s ‘Centre for Environment and Society,’ which provides events and networking opportunities. Person Specification Only UK domiciled applicants who meet the following criteria may apply: Not already have a Masters’ degree. Be from a low-income household background as evidenced by, for example, being in receipt of a full maintenance loan or Special Support loan during their undergraduate studies. and/or Be one of the following categories of ethnicity: Black African Black Caribbean Black Other Mixed – White and Black Caribbean Mixed – White and Black African Other mixed background (including Black African, Black Caribbean and Black Other) Funding Details Home tuition fee waiver. Living costs stipend at the UK Research and Innovation recommended level per year. The stipend for 2026-27 is £21,805. A research allowance of £10,000 (in total) to be spent on authorised research costs, for example supplies and equipment, fieldwork etc. Closing Date: 11:59 pm BST on Monday 14th September 2026

item.description: The Department of Humanities and Social Sciences at the Mushtaq Ahmad Gurmani School of Humanities and Social Sciences (MGSHSS), Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS), invites applications for a full-time, tenure-track faculty position (Assistant Professor or above) in Political Science. About the Role We are seeking candidates with expertise in Quantitative Research Methods who can teach in this area alongside core Political Science courses. The successful candidate will contribute to the department's two undergraduate degrees — BSc (Honours) in Political Science and BSc (Honours) in Politics and Economics - both of which encourage students to explore Pakistan and the broader globalized world through diverse theoretical and methodological perspectives in the Social Sciences generally, and Political Science specifically. While candidates will primarily teach undergraduate courses (three per academic year), they will also have the opportunity to teach in the Department's newly launched M.Phil. in Society, Culture, and Politics (SCP). Candidate Profile Candidates should have a specialization in one or two of the following subfields: Comparative Politics International Relations Political Economy Applicants should demonstrate: A strong interest in and commitment to undergraduate teaching in Pakistan An active research and publishing agenda in one of the fields listed above A commitment to institution-building and to the intellectual life of the department and university Requirements Candidates must have completed their PhD or submitted their dissertation at the time of application. This is a full-time, on-campus position requiring physical presence for in-person teaching. How to Apply Interested applicants should submit: A current curriculum vitae A cover letter The names of three referees to hssrecruitment@lums.edu.pk Deadline: September 6, 2026 Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

item.title: Research Associate, El-Erian Institute for Behavioural Economics and Public Policy (Fixed Term)
item.description: Are you a passionate behavioural scientist eager to make a real-world impact? Do you want to conduct cutting-edge research at one of the world's most celebrated universities? If so, this is an opportunity not to be missed. Cambridge Judge Business School is seeking a talented and motivated Research Associate to join the El-Erian Institute for Behavioural Economics and Public Policy. Situated at the heart of the Cambridge Cluster, Europe's most successful technology entrepreneurship hub, the Institute brings together world-class minds to explore the frontiers of behavioural science, economics, and public policy. Led by its inaugural Director, the El-Erian Professor of Behavioural Economics and Public Policy, the Institute is a vibrant, collaborative community of around ten core researchers, united by a shared ambition to generate knowledge that truly matters. In this role, you will be at the forefront of interdisciplinary research, contributing to the full research lifecycle, from study design and data collection through to analysis, interpretation, and publication in leading international journals. You will have the opportunity to shape your own research portfolio, engage with policymakers and external stakeholders, support the next generation of researchers, and contribute to funding applications that drive the Institute's ambitious agenda forward. This is not simply a research post, it is a platform from which to build a distinguished academic career. We are looking for someone who combines intellectual curiosity with rigorous analytical capability. You will hold a PhD in social psychology, behavioural economics, or a closely related discipline, and bring strong expertise in experimental and quantitative methods, including proficiency in Python and Bayesian analytical approaches. A track record of high-quality, impactful research publications that demonstrate a meaningful contribution to the field, experience of policy engagement, and the ability to collaborate across diverse teams will set you apart. Familiarity with AI and LLM-based research methods would be a welcome addition. This is a two-year fixed-term appointment, based at Trumpington Street, Cambridge, with hybrid working available. The role is full-time with a start date of 18 January 2027. Interviews are planned for week commencing 24 August 2026. To apply online for this vacancy and to view further information about the role, please click the 'Apply' button above. Informal queries may be directed to hrsupport@jbs.cam.ac.uk Please quote reference NS50509 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

item.title: Research Fellow, Sustainability and Resilience (focus on Social Issues)
item.description: About IMD The International Institute for Management Development (IMD) has been pioneering leadership development for nearly 80 years. Founded by business for business, we are an independent university institute with Swiss roots and global reach. Operating from Lausanne with strategic hubs in Singapore, Shenzhen, and Cape Town, IMD works with 19,000+ executives from 120+ countries annually. Our 145,000+ alumni form a powerful global network. Consistently ranked among the world's top business schools, IMD bridges cutting-edge research with real-world application to help leaders solve problems, scale solutions, and drive impact. Real Learning for Real Impact. To reinforce our team, we are looking for a Research Fellow, Sustainability and Resilience (focus on social issues) The Job’s mission The research fellow will work for the Risk & Resilience Initiative. The initiative is led by Prof. Florian Hoos and based on strong collaborations with Prof. Sophie Bacq and Prof. Karl Schmedders as well as a network of researchers from around the world. The main goal of the initiative is to bring the sustainability conversation back to the boardroom thereby ensuring the resilience and long-term value creation of firms. Concretely, this means helping corporate boards and investors integrate scientific knowledge (e.g., planetary boundaries, IPCC reports) and social foundations (e.g. what is at the core of Doughnut Economics) into corporate governance, opportunity and risk management. The initiative leverages IMD’s strengths in applied and scientific research, innovative executive education learning format development, and global dissemination, all based on strong partnerships, to maximize impact and longevity of the initiative. The Research Fellow will contribute to the initiative through developing and conducting novel and relevant research that fulfils the goals of the initiative, and is publishable in top-tier academic journals and relevant for practitioner outlets such that it can generate an impact beyond academia, particularly towards board members and investors. Publication formats therefore include academic- and practitioner-oriented articles, literature reviews, reports, and case studies. The research fellow should also ensure the successful completion of the publication process, and contribute to translating research results into materials for IMD teaching offerings, engagement platforms, and events. Key deliverables The aim of the Research Fellow’s work is to generate and disseminate impactful outcomes for both academic and practitioner audiences: Develop a clear research strategy in line with the initiative and publish in FT50 journals whereby we see value in both FT50-practitioner-oriented journals such as Harvard Business Review, and the more research oriented journals. We also see value in high impact journals such as Nature Sustainability or comparable journals. Distill key insights from the conducted research and publish white papers, cases, and other publication formats that reach a broader audience. Leverage various dissemination channels to communicate and translate the research insights into short communication formats. Engage stakeholders and gain partners for the initiative that support the research, and help disseminating the produced knowledge. Foster engagement with scholars across the globe for future impactful research dedicated to the objective of the initiative. Contribute to strategy development for the initiative that guarantees its long-term success Ideal profile Academic background: PhD in management, sociology, political science, economics, sustainable finance or a related field, with a clear focus on social impact aspects of sustainability for business, and ideally the interaction of social and environmental dimensions. The quality of the PhD should be proven through high quality working papers, or ideally through RRs or publications in top-tier academic journals such as FT50 journals. Substantive expertise: Evidence of research or fieldwork in one or more of the following areas is essential: Social impact measurement, Sustainability reporting, Sustainability strategy, human rights, dough not economics or further sustainability topics that focus on the social dimensions of sustainability and that are relevant to top managers and boards. Knowledge of sustainability reporting standards (CSRD, ISSB, GRI etc.) and frameworks is a plus. Methods: Strong qualitative (interviews, process tracing, case study design) and/or quantitative skills (econometrics, panel/archival data, field experiments, text analytics). Mixed‑methods experience is a plus. Output orientation: Demonstrated capacity to publish in top-tier academic journals and ideally also in practitioner outlets and other high outreach formats. Professionalism: Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, ideally proven in interactions with high- level audiences (managers, politicians, executive education settings) Stakeholder engagement: Comfort engaging top managers and board members with different backgrounds and from different cultures. Attitude: Ability to work independently and proactively with minimum supervision. Collaborative and capable of working in a multi-disciplinary environment. Deadline and results oriented Language: Full fluency in English (written and spoken) is a must. Proficiency in French and/or German is helpful but not a requirement. Research Fellow Location: Lausanne, Switzerland or remotely Salary: Depending on experience and location Hours: Full Time (40 hours) or Part Time (minimum 20 hours) Contract Type: 3 years, Fixed-Term Closes: 06.09.2026 Start Date: ASAP How to apply If you have the above skills and would like to work in our stimulating environment, please send your complete application file (letter of motivation and resume in English, copies of your work certificates and diplomas) before September 6th 2026 via the above ' Apply ' button. If you’re a qualified candidate with a disability (such as dyslexia, sight and/or hearing disabilities, etc) and you need a reasonable accommodation in order to apply for this position, please specify it in your application. A valid Swiss work permit or Swiss or EU-25EFTA citizenship is required for this position.

item.title: Tenure-Track Associate Professor / Assistant Professor in International Relations
item.description: Applications are invited for appointment as Tenure-Track Associate Professor / Assistant Professor in International Relations in the Department of Politics and Public Administration (Ref: 536865), to commence in August 2027 or at another mutually agreed time, on a three-year fixed-term basis, with the possibility of renewal and consideration for tenure before the expiry of a second three-year fixed-term contract, both subject to satisfactory performance. Exceptionally outstanding candidates at the Associate Professor level may be considered for appointment on direct tenure terms subject to the University's approval. The Department of Politics and Public Administration is an internationally oriented research-focused department that covers a broad range of fields in Political Science and Public Administration. The Department offers three highly successful taught postgraduate programmes - Master in International and Public Affairs (MIPA), Master of Public Administration (MPA) and Doctor of Public Administration (DPA) - as well as a thriving undergraduate programme. More information about the Department can be found at https://ppa.hku.hk/ . Applicants should hold a Ph.D. degree by the time of appointment and demonstrate excellence in research and teaching. The Department welcomes applications from excellent candidates who specialise in any field of International Relations and is eager to both consolidate its existing strengths and to diversify into new areas of research and teaching. A highly competitive salary commensurate with qualifications and experience will be offered, in addition to annual leave and medical benefits. At the current rates, salaries tax does not exceed 15% of the gross income. The appointment will attract a contract-end gratuity and University contribution to a retirement benefits scheme, totalling up to 15% of the basic salary. Housing benefits will be provided as applicable. The University only accepts online applications for the above post. Applicants should apply online at the University’s careers site (via the above ' Apply ' button) and upload (1) an up-to-date CV, (2) a letter of interest, (3) graduate transcripts where relevant, (4) a research statement, (5) a teaching statement, (6) teaching evaluations where available, and (7) the contact information of three referees. Please also arrange for your referees’ letters of support to be sent directly to us at ppahr@hku.hk. We would be glad to receive these letters from Interfolio, your department administration or the referees themselves. Review of applications will begin on October 1, 2026. Further inquiries may be made to the Head of Department, Professor Robert Thomson, rthomson@hku.hk . The University is an equal opportunities employer and is committed to equality, ethics, inclusivity, diversity and transparency.

item.title: Programme Coordinator, Huth Initiative for a New Political Economy
item.description: This is a fixed-term appointment, with possibility of extension. The Programme Coordinator will play a key role in ensuring the smooth running of the Huth Initiative for a New Political Economy, a major new research programme at LSE that brings together leading academics to develop the ideas, policies and institutions for a fairer and more cohesive economic system. Working closely with the Programme Manager, the post holder will provide high-quality administrative, financial and logistical support across all areas of the programme’s work, including research, policy engagement and events. They will also serve as Executive Assistant to the Director (Sir Tim Besley), Executive Director (Dr Daniel Chandler) and Policy Director (Professor Richard Davies), supporting diary management, correspondence and meeting coordination. This is a varied and dynamic role, well suited to an organised, motivated and collegial individual who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and is excited by the mission of the Huth Initiative to shape a new political economy for the twenty-first century. As part of a small and growing team, the post holder will have the opportunity to shape new ways of working and help build a major new Initiative from the ground up, requiring an entrepreneurial spirit and a flexible, hands-on approach. The successful candidate will have: Experience in administrative, financial or events support roles, ideally within a higher-education or research environment. Excellent organisational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with confidence dealing with senior academics and external stakeholders. Ability to work independently with limited supervision and as part of a small, collaborative team. We offer an occupational pension scheme, generous annual leave and excellent training and development opportunities. Closing Date : 10 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates The closing time for receipt of applications is 23.59 UK time. Regrettably, we are unable to accept any late applications. item.title: Local party organiser
item.description: As Local Party Organiser, you will support the Liberal Democrats across Ely and East Cambridgeshire so that: membership and the volunteer base grow; fundraising capacity increases to support local campaigning, including by the MP; we are better placed to fight elections, with campaigning and communications well coordinated; more Liberal Democrats are elected to the new unitary authority; we increase our majority at the next Parliamentary election. Priorities will be set by the local executive and campaign strategy team, with regional staff. Key responsibilities Support the campaign committee in strategic planning and organisation. Recruit, train, manage and motivate volunteers, and lead teams across doorstep, phone, online and delivery activity. Plan and deliver a sustained programme of doorstep and telephone voter contact. Oversee and contribute to campaign literature, and build our digital campaigning capacity. Manage campaign data and organise volunteers to do the same, in line with data protection rules. Liaise with the regional party, neighbouring local parties and council groups. Support the fundraising group as duties allow. Carry out other duties your line manager may reasonably require. You will also observe health and safety rules, uphold professional standards, promote equal opportunities and diversity, and take part in relevant training. Person specification Essential A strong self-starter, able to work unsupervised, manage your own workload, prioritise and meet deadlines. A can-do attitude and resilience under pressure. The ability to communicate effectively, in writing and in person, with a wide variety of people. The ability to motivate, manage and delegate to a team, and to work well within one. A willingness to learn new skills, software and ways of working. Sympathy with the aims and values of the Liberal Democrats. Desirable Knowledge of the local area and its politics. The ability to produce effective political literature. Experience of managing volunteers and running election campaigns. Good digital skills, including experience of, or willingness to learn, Connect, Lighthouse and Affinity Publisher. An eye for issues with campaigning potential, and confidence with local media. A full UK driving licence and access to a vehicle. item.description: Epilepsy Society is a dynamic charity with ambitious plans to revolutionise the lives of people through advocacy, research and care. item.description: About the Role As Policy and Public Affairs Adviser, you will support the Electoral Commission's policy and public affairs work in Wales. This externally focused role sits at the heart of policy, legislation and democratic engagement. Working with Welsh Government officials, Members of the Senedd, political stakeholders and colleagues across the Commission, you will help shape the organisation's response to developments affecting elections and democracy in Wales. Key responsibilities include: Researching and analysing political, policy and legislative developments. Supporting engagement with Welsh Government consultations and legislation. Drafting consultation responses, briefings and policy papers. Building and maintaining stakeholder relationships. Supporting events and public affairs activity. Preparing advice for colleagues and supporting post-election reporting. About the Team You'll join a supportive team leading the Commission's work in Wales. The team works across policy, public affairs, electoral administration, regulation and stakeholder engagement, helping ensure the Commission remains a trusted voice on democratic issues. Who We're Looking For We're seeking a politically aware individual with strong analytical, communication and relationship-building skills. You'll be able to demonstrate: Experience in policy, public affairs or stakeholder engagement. Strong research and analytical skills. Ability to communicate complex information clearly. Experience building effective stakeholder relationships. Strong influencing skills and sound political judgement. Experience drafting reports, briefings or policy papers. Excellent communication skills and attention to detail. Welsh language skills are desirable. Why Work for Us? The successful candidate will support policy development and deliver political engagement to advance the interests of the UK publishing industry. Responsibilities • Deliver effective public affairs engagement, including supporting a programme of work for the APPG on Publishing, Parliamentary Book Club and other parliamentary activity. • Monitor political and policy developments across Westminster and Whitehall, providing timely analysis and updates to colleagues and members. • Contribute to policy development by undertaking research and drafting material, including for Select Committee responses and letters to ministers. • Draft content for speeches, briefings and articles for the senior team on policy issues. • Build relationships with publisher members and network with counterparts at other trade associations and partner organisations. • Assist with the effective running of the Policy & Public Affairs team and wider Publishers Association, including providing the secretariat to a number of sector councils, organising and contributing to member meetings, and other administrative matters. • Work with colleagues on planning, project managing and evaluating our work in a way that enables reporting to members. item.title: Campaigns Manager (Western Counties)
item.description: Lead and deliver winning campaigns in priority areas across the Western Counties, directly managing key contests where required and ensuring campaigns are professional, compliant and strategically focused. Work closely with MPs, candidates, councillors and local party teams to run structured campaign planning meetings, set clear objectives and drive progress against voter contact, fundraising and organisational targets. Build sustainable, self-sufficient campaign teams in held seats by strengthening volunteer recruitment, leadership capacity, and local fundraising. Develop campaign-ready infrastructure in emerging priority seats, including clear strategy, messaging frameworks, data-led targeting and measurable growth plans. Support and develop local organisers and campaign staff through mentoring, training and where agreed line management, helping to grow a confident and capable regional team. Embed best practice in data, digital campaigning, literature production and compliance across the region. The ability to analyse data and voter insight to inform targeting, messaging and resource allocation. Strong leadership skills, with experience motivating volunteers or staff, building effective teams and building positive relationships with stakeholders. item.title: Caseworker
item.description: Cat Smith is seeking a motivated, organised and compassionate Caseworker to join her constituency team in Lancaster on a full-time basis (37.5 hours per week). This is an exciting opportunity to make a difference to people’s lives by supporting residents with issues including housing, immigration, welfare, health, education, and local government services. The successful candidate will be committed to delivering excellent public service, able to work sensitively with people facing difficult circumstances, and capable of managing a varied and demanding caseload. You’ll join a friendly and supportive team working from the constituency office in Lancaster, with some opportunities to support Parliamentary duties in Westminster. While flexibility is important, this is not a hybrid role. Staff may, by agreement, work from home on an ad hoc basis where operationally appropriate. This flexibility is intended to support occasional needs rather than regular home-working. Key responsibilities Manage a caseload of constituency enquiries from receipt to resolution Correspond with constituents by telephone, email, letter and in person Liaise with government departments, local authorities, public bodies and other organisations on behalf of constituents Answer routine telephone calls from constituents, offer advice and support, maintaining a calm, empathetic manner when dealing with challenging calls Draft clear, accurate and empathetic correspondence Research policy and legislation where required to support casework Maintain accurate case records using a casework management system Assist with constituency surgeries and community events Ensure all work complies with GDPR, parliamentary standards and office procedures Essential skills and experience Excellent written and verbal communication skills Strong organisational skills and ability to prioritise competing demands Sound judgement and attention to detail Ability to work professionally with confidential and sensitive information Excellent IT skills, including Microsoft Office Commitment to delivering outstanding public service Ability to work independently and in a small team Desirable Previous casework or support service experience Experience working with public sector bodies, charities or elected representatives Knowledge of Lancaster and Wyre and local community issues Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 9 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Anticipated interviews: Monday 17 August 2026 in Lancaster. Cat Smith MP is an equal opportunities employer and welcomes applications from candidates from all backgrounds and communities. Selection will be based solely on merit. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Application Details Please submit: A CV (maximum two pages); and A covering letter (maximum two pages) explaining how your skills and experience meet the requirements of the role. Applications should be sent by email to cat.smith.mp@parliament.uk Website : http://www.catsmith.co.uk

item.title: Full-Time Caseworker
item.description: Contract: Full time (37.5 hours p/w) Elsie is looking for a full-time caseworker to work in her busy constituency office. The successful applicant will be happy to work both independently and as part of Elsie’s small, close-knit team. The role will be full-time and will allow for hybrid working both in the constituency office in Heywood, and remotely. Duties include: - Manage a large number of standard queries and more complex cases from members of the public. - Answering the telephone to constituents and handling incoming voicemails, and other correspondence. - Gather relevant information to assist with resolving cases. - Log all cases, monitor progress and ensure all identified actions are taken. - Ensure records are kept and information managed confidentially in line with GDPR. - Draft high-quality responses to constituents. - Identify key themes emerging from casework and communicate these to the MP to raise in Parliament. - Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately, in accordance with the MPs requirements. - Assist at surgeries and other meetings and follow up as appropriate. - Develop and maintain systems that ensure proactive communication with constituents - for example, street letters. - Support with the organisation of constituency events and wider constituency engagement. - There will be a requirement to occasionally work outside of normal working hours, including attending events with the MP as required. Essential Criteria: - Previous experience working as a caseworker in a similar, public-facing role. - Ability to deal with and prioritise a large and varied workload and work well under pressure. - Ability to manage expectations in sometimes challenging circumstances. - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills. - Good IT skills including MS Office. - Ability to draft letters and emails to a high professional standard. - Motivation to work proactively and independently, as well as part of a small team. - Commitment to the aims and values of the Labour Party The role will focus on casework related to housing so knowledge and experience of housing casework would be desirable. Elsie welcomes applications from everyone regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, faith, disability or background. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 14 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Shortlisted candidates will be interviewed on Friday 21st August in Heywood. Ideally the candidate should be able to start on Monday 7th September, or very soon after. Application Details To apply please send your CV and 1 side A4 cover letter to: elsie.blundell.mp@parliament.uk by 12 noon on the closing date. You will only be contacted if you are successfully short-listed. Website : http://www.elsieblundell.org.uk

item.title: Graduate Consultant
item.description: The insights to advise and the relationships to deliver are built from the moment you enter the workplace. That’s why Lowick Hedry is launching Graduate Kick Start. Graduate Kick Start takes a graduate and turns them into an adviser who can work across all four of our practices – built environment, infrastructure, litigation & crisis, and public affairs – in twelve months. This isn’t a shadowing scheme. From week one you’re doing real, billable work for real clients, with the support in place to make sure you’re never out of your depth and the stretch to make sure you’re never coasting. You’ll also learn to use AI properly from the very start, through our in-house Vanguard programme. How you’ll be supported: A Personal Development Plan. Lowick Hedry Academy. A buddy for the day-to-day. Quarterly reviews against a competency framework spanning all four practices. What we’re looking for: A creative thinker and a clear writer. A real interest in politics, policy, and social issues. Experience making a difference in the world around us. Ownership and initiative whether in work, studies, or extracurricular. Complete the programme and you move into a permanent Consultant role, on a path to running your own accounts. Closing Date : 12 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Start Date: Autumn 2026 Application Details Please submit your CV and cover letter via our website by 6pm on the closing date. Please send any questions to graduatekickstart@lowickhedry.com http://lowickhedry.com/graduatekickstart/ Website : http://lowickhedry.com
