item.title: Two Research Officer/PhD Posts
item.description: The University of Tübingen is one of Europe’s oldest universities and in recent years has been very successful in the German federal and state governments’ Excellence Initiative. The Research Unit Comparative Public Policy at the Institute of Political Science of the University of Tübingen invites applications for Two Research Officer/PhD Posts (German public sector pay scheme TV-L E13, 75%) for the duration of 3 years from 1 November 2026 (or as soon as possible thereafter). Gross annual salary is commensurate with experience starting from approximately 43,000 Euro. The successful candidates will contribute to the externally funded research project “Measuring the Past and Assessing Future Possibilities of Welfare State Dualization” (DFG, German Research Foundation). Essential requirements: Excellent undergraduate and graduate degree in political science, sociology, or social policy Interest in and knowledge of comparative welfare state research and/or attitudinal research Excellent communication, presentation and writing skills in English (additional German, Swedish, Polish, and/or Italian language skills are beneficial) Excellent skills in qualitative and quantitative methods Excellent intercultural communication skills Ability to work both independently and as part of a team Disabled persons will be preferred in case of equal qualification. The University seeks to raise the number of women in research and teaching and therefore encourages qualified women academics to apply for these positions. If you are interested in this position, please send your application with the usual documentation (letter of motivation, curriculum vitae, copies of certificates, publication list or writing sample, etc.) in electronic form (one PDF file only) to: jakub.sowula@uni-tuebingen.de via the above 'Apply' button. Deadline for applications is 24.08.2026 (noon CEST) . Interviews are scheduled for 22 September 2026. For further questions, please contact: jakub.sowula@uni-tuebingen.de or martin.seeleib-kaiser@uni-tuebingen.de
item.dc:creator: Universität Tübingen

item.title: Post-doctoral Research Fellow Level 2 - Temporary Fixed Term up to March 2030 (Part-Time 0.6FTE)
item.description: Applications are invited for a temporary part-time (0.6FTE) post of a UCD Post-doctoral Research Fellow Level 2 within UCD School of Politics and International Relations. The School of Politics and International Relations at University College Dublin invites applications for a Senior Postdoctoral Research Fellow Level 2 position on the Horizon Europe-funded project QUEST: The European Union's Quest for a Relational Open Strategic Autonomy. The successful candidate will contribute primarily to Work Package 10 (Defence Policy and Procurement) and associated cross-project activities examining the European Union's pursuit of Open Strategic Autonomy (OSA) in the fields of defence industrial policy, defence procurement and security governance. The postholder will undertake original research on EU defence policy instruments, defence-industrial cooperation, procurement frameworks, and the evolving relationship between strategic autonomy, economic security and European defence integration. Working under the supervision of the Principal Investigator, the researcher will contribute to comparative case studies, stakeholder engagement, academic publications, policy outputs and consortium-wide analytical activities. Closing date: 12:00 noon (local Irish time) on 18 th August 2026. Applications must be submitted by the closing date and time specified. Any applications which are still in progress at the closing time of 12:00 noon (Local Irish Time) on the specified closing date will be cancelled automatically by the system. UCD are unable to accept late applications. UCD do not require assistance from Recruitment Agencies. Any CVs submitted by Recruitment Agencies will be returned. The PD2 post is intended for researchers who have completed PD1. As with the PD1, if you have already completed your PD2 stage in UCD or will soon complete a PD2, or your total Postdoctoral experience, inclusive of the duration of the advertised post, would exceed 6 years, you should not apply and should refer to Research Fellow posts instead. Prior to application, further information (including application procedure) should be obtained from the Work at UCD website: www.ucd.ie/workatucd/jobs

item.title: Administrative Officer
item.description: Noah Law MP is looking for a skilled Administrative Officer to join his team. The successful candidate will support Noah’s constituency and Parliamentary work across St Austell and Newquay, through the triage and action of emails, telephone calls and social media enquiries, handling general enquiries, taking actions and minutes of meetings, and ensuring overall administrative efficiency in the office. This will include management of some casework in support of Casework staff, at times managing a small caseload of their own, and joining the MP in attending events or visiting constituents. They will also take responsibility for the administration and organisation of events and security apparatus as required, and keep track of invoices and receipts. The role will be based either in the constituency office or London office, following negotiation upon successful offer of the role. The successful candidate will report directly to the Office Manager, with other delegating of some tasks from the Parliamentary Assistant and Noah. The successful candidate will be highly organised, proactive, and dedicated to supporting a busy MP in a fast-paced environment. They will have a commitment to the Labour Party and its aims and values, and shall also be knowledgeable of Noah’s areas of interest. The role also involves general office duties such as answering calls, coordinating with external agencies, and drafting complex correspondence. The successful candidate should be able to handle enquiries efficiently, prioritise competing demands, and take initiative within a busy office setting. While the focus shall be administrative duties, the successful applicant will support other duties where required. There may be a requirement to work outside of the normal working hours and travel for visits occasionally, including supporting with constituency surgeries. This role is a full time role (40 hours per week) until March 31st, 2027, in the first instance. Extensions to the contract will be subject to other factors. Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 16 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates The advert will close at 23:59 on Friday, 21st August. Interviews will take place on a rolling basis, no later than Wednesday 26th August. Start Date: ASAP after Thursday 20th August. Must be available no later than Monday, 21st September. Application Details Further information on the role, as well as how to apply, can be found on our website: https://noahlaw.co.uk/careers/ Applications will only be accepted through the online form linked to on Noah's website. Website : http://www.noahlaw.co.uk Additional Notes 01/08/26- closing date changed from the 21/08 to the 16/08

item.title: Senior Caseworker
item.description: Claire Hazelgrove MP is looking for a committed and organised Senior Caseworker to join her constituency office. The Senior Caseworker will support Claire to be an active, impactful and approachable MP. You will lead the casework function and work with a Caseworker to provide advice and support to local people on a range of issues. Managing a large caseload, organising MP advice surgeries, and supporting relevant events, you will help resolve problems for local people through communication with government agencies, local authorities, the voluntary sector and other organisations. Holding a senior role in the team, and working with others, you will collate and surface trends which can inform wider policy change efforts of the MP and team. Key Responsibilities: Lead and oversee the casework and wider direct resident support function of the team Deal with large numbers of standard queries, as well as leading on the more complex individual cases - by phone, email, or face to face - in a professional, confidential, caring and sensitive manner Ensure that each case is dealt with promptly, sensitively, confidentially and accurately in accordance with the MP Plan and organise MP advice surgeries, including identifying and booking residents in for appointments, arranging appropriate venues across the constituency Identify and surface trends and produce relevant reports on issues faced by residents, working across the team to support policy change and campaigning efforts led by others in the team on these, and reporting back to residents Support the Caseworker in their continued growth and development Work collaboratively across the team on relevant project work to help residents more easily access support and to highlight the impact of casework in supporting residents Required skills and values: Ability to deal with and prioritise a large and varied caseload, and work well under pressure Ability to manage expectations in sometimes challenging circumstances Excellent interpersonal and written communication skills Ability to work independently as well as effectively as part of a small team Ability and willingness to work outside of normal hours and travel for work occasionally Discretion and professionalism Sympathetic to the aims, values and objectives of the Labour Party Desirable skills Previous casework experience Upon appointment you will be required to comply with the Baseline Personnel Security Standard, undertaken by the Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO). See Members’ Staff Verification Office (MSVO) page for further info. MPs generally pay staff in accordance with IPSA guidelines . Closing Date : 5 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Closing Date: Noon on Wednesday 5th August 2026 Interviews: Friday 7th August 2026 Start date: To be agreed, and based on notice period, but as soon as possible Due to the high volume of expected applications we are only able to contact you if you have been shortlisted. Thank you. Application Details Please send a relevant CV and one page covering letter outlining how you meet the job specification and your interest in the role to: clairehazelgrovemp@gmail.com quoting ‘Senior Caseworker Application - Your First and Last Name’ in the subject line. Ensuring high quality speechwriting support for the Chair and Chief Executive, through the effective leadership of other experts and sometimes playing a hands-on personal role. item.title: Policy and Advocacy Intern
item.description: The Gregson Family Foundation (GFF) is a small family foundation focussed on grant-giving in three areas: the environment, young people in Britain and social justice. In recent years, the Foundation has devoted significant time, and the majority of its grant-giving, to the #BeeWell programme. The successful applicant should have an understanding of, and empathy with, the issues that young people in England face as well as an interest in wellbeing, an appreciation of central/local government structures and an interest in national politics and political decision making. The postholder should have excellent communication skills (both written and verbal); be comfortable engaging with stakeholders with different interests; be a self-starter but comfortable working as part of a small, close-knit team. The postholder is likely to be a recent (possibly Masters) graduate with an interest in, and experience of, the areas above. This internship will work with David Gregson, in particular, to both undertake specific GFF funded projects and support #BeeWell's efforts to expand its footprint and influence policy affecting young people's wellbeing. Specific duties of the post holder: 1. Keep up to date with policy and political developments and develop expertise as required. This might involve contact with e.g. MPs offices, select committees, APPGs, think tanks etc. 2. Execute administrative functions (e.g. meeting notes and follow-up emails) as needed and requested 3. Support, as necessary, GFF funded programmatic work across Greater Manchester 4. Work with, coordinate and contribute to new research being started in the Autumn by a GFF funded Research Fellow. 5. Support GFF’s growing focus on the Isle of Wight as a specific area that could become an exemplar of what is possible 6. Support continuing policy work by GFF and #BeeWell with, as examples, The Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes, the current Milburn Review, the Department for Education and others 7. Assist Chair with writing papers/publications as well as wider social media posts and other communication efforts including possibly podcasts. https://beewellprogramme.org/the-gregson-family-foundation-is-hiring-a-new-policy-and-advocacy-intern/ Closing Date : 10 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates The closing date/time for applications will be at the end of normal business hours on Monday 10 August . Virtual interviews will take place on Thursday 27 August . We intend that the successful applicant will, if possible, start around the middle of September. Application Details To express your interest in this role, please email Frances East on frances@davidjgregson.com with a copy of your cv (or bio) and a covering letter setting out why you are interested in the role. https://beewellprogramme.org/the-gregson-family-foundation-is-hiring-a-new-policy-and-advocacy-intern/ Website : https://gregsonfoundation.org.uk/

item.title: Head of Parliamentary Engagement - International Development
item.description: We are hiring a Head of Parliamentary Engagement to build and run our parliamentary work and deliver sustained engagement in Westminster. You will own our relationships across both Houses, building an organised parliamentary base and making sure our analysis reaches the right people. This is a role for an energetic organiser who can get people into rooms and maintain a complex network. Key responsibilities • Build and manage a network of supportive MPs, Peers and staffers. • Coordinate parliamentary activity: letters, questions, debates and meetings. • Set up and run parliamentary groups, including possible APPG secretariat work. • Organise briefings and meetings with parliamentarians, Ministers, Special Advisers and officials; liaise between them and our experts. • Plan and deliver parliamentary events - roundtables, dinners, receptions, panels - with faith groups, NGOs, sector partners, plus activity at party conference. • Monitor parliamentary business; identify opportunities to intervene. • Distribute briefings to parliamentarians and staff, timed to the parliamentary calendar; keep accurate records. Flexibility You will at times take on tasks beyond your core brief, occasionally work outside office hours, and travel to events outside London such as party conference. Time off compensates for out-of-hours work. Person specification Essential • Experience in or with Parliament: for an MP or Peer, in public affairs, an APPG or campaign secretariat, or an advocacy organisation. • Track record of building productive relationships with parliamentarians and staff. • Strong understanding of the Labour Party, its people, culture and internal politics. We work cross-party, but our centre of gravity is Labour. • Excellent organisational skills; the ability to run several strands of work to the parliamentary timetable. • Clear, concise writing for correspondence and briefings. • Discretion; our work depends on trust. • Self-starting and comfortable with autonomy in a small team. • The right to work in the UK. • Sympathy with the aims and values of the Labour Party and trade union movement. Desirable • Knowledge of international development, climate and the global picture. • Experience organising events in Parliament. • Experience of campaign organising: political, union, civil society. Closing Date : 7 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates The closing time for applications is 9.00am. First interviews will be online in w/c 10 August. Second interviews will follow in person in Central London. We do not expect to appoint before the closing date. We expect the successful applicant to start in September but are flexible given notice periods. Application Details Send a CV and short cover letter (1 page) to mike@ukeucommission.org . Applications will be considered as received; an early appointment may be made. We will only be able to contact shortlisted candidates. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We are aware of the under-representation of some groups in politics and the development sector, and we would particularly welcome applications from candidates from those backgrounds. If you have questions prior to submission please contact Mike Buckley at the email above. Website : https://www.ukeucommission.org

item.title: Content Officer
item.description: PoliMonitor is growing its content team and is looking for a Content Officer to join us. This is an entry level role with a particular focus on our Scotland content offering, following our launch this year of PoliMonitor Scotland, alongside broader UK parliamentary monitoring. About the Role You'll help deliver the political monitoring and intelligence our clients rely on, covering parliamentary business across Westminster and the Scottish Parliament, including House of Commons and House of Lords committees and Scottish Parliament proceedings. You will also support the continued growth of PoliMonitor Scotland. You'll build knowledge across a broad range of policy areas that our clients follow closely, including energy, health, technology, transport and housing, alongside a strong grounding in parliamentary processes and exposure to the public affairs industry. Key responsibilities Support the monitoring and summarising of parliamentary proceedings across Westminster and the Scottish Parliament, including committees, chamber business and FMQs, to keep clients informed of what matters to them. Contribute to the maintenance and writing of biographies for MPs, MSPs and Peers, building the political intelligence clients rely on to understand key stakeholders. item.title: PhD Studentship - Narratives of Enslavement and their Legacies
item.description: Start date: February 2027 King’s College London’s Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War is pleased to announce the availability of a fully funded AHRC doctoral studentship from October 2026, to be jointly supervised across the English and War Studies departments by Dr. Michael Collins(English) and Dr. Maeve Ryan (War Studies). We invite proposals under the theme of: “Narratives of Enslavement and their Legacies” Project scope and research questions Applicants are invited to propose innovative research exploring any element of the relationship between narratives of slavery broadly defined (including post-enslavement life-writing and the “slave narrative” genre; the legacies of enslavement in fiction and the transatlantic literary traditions; and critical theories of race and racialisation emerging from histories of enslavement and indenture) written in English between the period of 1776 and the mid twentieth century. Due to the specialisms of the proposed supervisors, focus on the British Empire and the U.S. is preferred, but modes of transnational engagement and comparativist readings across national and linguistic traditions are highly encouraged. Since the candidate will be situated across two faculties, The Department of English and the Department of War Studies, an interest in questions of how geopolitical conflict, conflict-based diasporic movement, and the conditions of war have affected and shaped narrative traditions would be an advantage. The LCRSW is driven by a singular, transformative vision: to learn from the past in order fundamentally to change how the world understands, forecasts, and tackles the enduring problem of slavery in war. How, where and why has slavery in war emerged over time? How has slavery influenced the course, conduct, and consequences of war? How have slavery and war shaped the evolution of legal and normative frameworks throughout history? What are the needs of survivors of slavery in conflict? Consequently, potential methodological and conceptual areas of interest for proposals may include (but are not limited to) readings of narratives of enslavement through theories of: Racial Capitalism (Robinson) Narratology Environmental Humanities/ The Plantationcene (McKittrick) Ontologies and “Genres” of the Human (Wynter) Transnationalism Human Rights and Legal Frameworks British Studies, American Studies, Settler Colonial Studies, Multicultural Studies It is expected that the candidate will have strong skills in use of archives (identifying and defining their archival focus will be a major element of the first year of the doctorate) and a willingness to engage in forms of public outreach work appropriate to their research, in conjunction with the ‘Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War' and The Department of English. The studentship can be taken up either full or part-time. Students should have an excellent academic record. A master’s degree in a relevant subject (such as Literature, History, American Studies, War Studies, Development Studies, Anthropology, Cultural Studies) is a requirement. If you are unsure about the appropriateness of your disciplinary training, please reach out to either potential supervisor to discuss the proposal in advance. Details of award The award pays UKRI Home Tuition Fees (£5,238 for 2026/27) for PhD students. The award pays full maintenance for all students both home and international. The UKRI Doctoral Stipend for 2026/2027 is £21,805, plus a London Weighting of £2,000/year, plus Collaborative Activity funding at a rate of £600/year. Further details can be found on the UKRI website: www.ukri.org/manage-your award/studentship-guidance/support-for-ukri-funded-students The student is eligible to receive an additional Research Training Support Grant (RTSG) during the course of the project The project can be undertaken on a full-time or part-time basis. Eligibility This studentship is open to both Home and International applicants. However, the CRSW is limited to one Overseas studentship across the opportunities currently advertised. We are committed to welcoming applications from students from all backgrounds. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian, minority ethnic (BAME) backgrounds as they are currently underrepresented at this level in this discipline. We require an upper-second class (2:1) honours degree and a Master’s degree at high merit or above in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD (or international equivalent). Please see here for the English-language requirements for PhD students in the Department of War Studies (Band B): Postgraduate English language entry requirements | King's College London Assessment of applicants Applicants will be assessed by how well they meet the person specification for this position. This may include: An educational and research background that matches this research project. The potential to work effectively and inclusively with a diverse team of people The potential to take initiative and manage a dynamic and complex workload. The potential to develop expertise in new areas related to this subject. A demonstrated interest in and understanding of the proposed area of research, including knowledge of current challenges and opportunities. The potential to undertake continuous personal and professional development. The potential to communicate ideas and findings, verbally and in writing, clearly and effectively. An understanding of relevant research methods. How to apply If you have questions about the project or the application process, please contact Kelsey Carthew at crsw@kcl.ac.uk Applicants should apply at the link below and submit the following no later than 5pm on 1 st September 2026: qualtrics.kcl.ac.uk/jfe/form/SV_0UQML35ytEOvOHc Curriculum vitae A personal statement outlining your reasons for pursuing doctoral research at King’s College London A research proposal (5-10 pages in length) that explains your proposed area of focus; primary research question; importance and originality of your topic; initial thoughts on methods and potential case studies; and your familiarity with the existing literature and research on this topic. A sample of academic writing. If you are a current MA student awaiting results of your dissertation, please upload your submitted dissertation as your writing sample. Transcripts of undergraduate and master’s qualifications One academic reference Please submit all materials in English. Use of AI: While we recognise that AI tools can be useful for certain tasks, your application should reflect your own thinking, research interests, skills, and experience rather than AI generated content. Applications that rely heavily on AI-generated content may not demonstrate the originality, critical thinking, and personal insight expected for doctoral study. Please note it is the responsibility of applicants to request references from their referees and ensure that they have been received by this deadline. All documents should be submitted in either MS Word or PDF format. Interviews will be held in September with offers expected by the end of the month. Following the interview, the successful candidate will also need to formally apply to King’s College London and satisfy its admission requirements.

item.title: PhD Studentship - Slavery and the Seven Years’ War within and across the Caribbean Archipelago
item.description: Start date: February 2027 King’s College London’s Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War is pleased to announce the availability of a fully funded AHRC doctoral studentship from October 2026, to be jointly supervised across the History and War Studies departments. We invite proposals under the theme of: “Slavery and the Seven Years’ War within and across the Caribbean Archipelago” Project Scope and Research Questions This doctoral project will explore the relationships between military conflict and slavery in the context of the Seven Years’ War (1756-1763), often characterised as the first global war. The Seven Years’ War has generally been understood as a top-down military conflict between European powers, played out on a global stage. Displacing this traditional understanding of centre and periphery, this thesis will trace participation in the war from the ground up by individuals, networks, companies and colonial operators across notional imperial divides. The primary research object is to resituate slavery as both a core constituent and production of military conflict. While slavery has figured in important accounts of the Seven Years War, particularly for the contemporaneous occurrence of important ‘slave revolts’ such as Tacky’s War (1760-61), this thesis will be the first to conceptualise the relationship between slavery and war at the heart of this global conflict. Within this broad area of inquiry, applicants may propose their own area of focus, primary research questions, conceptual frameworks, methodological approaches and case studies. Projects with a transnational and multilingual focus are encouraged. Some important questions or topics this thesis might explore include: 1. Enslaved labour in the military: the official and unofficial presence of enslaved people dispatched by Caribbean plantation owners as island deployments and contributions to colonial military forces. 2. The impact of the Seven Years’ War on trafficking and trade with West Africa (including on the internal politics of precolonial West Africa) 3. The experiences of enslaved people, whose lives were shaped and influenced by military conflict. Thinking through survival, military experience and the conditions of war can reshape records of enslaved lives, more often understood as ‘freedom narratives’ and ‘fugitive archives’. 4. Abolitionism and the reinterpretation of slavery as a political, legal, and moral conundrum in the context of war. The thesis will use records across company and colonial archives: the East India Company and the Royal African Company, as well as papers in the National Archives Colonial Office Series, the Prize Papers, and the records of the High Court of Admiralty. As a critical historical case study in the deeper (re)conceptualisation of slavery and war at the heart of the Leverhulme Centre for Slavery in War, this project will have important implications for longer durée histories of slavery, colonialism, and empire. The candidate recruited to this role will be supported to participate in this collaborative research programme. They will be expected to contribute research to central datasets, and will be encouraged and supported to develop high-profile publications at the cutting edge, interdisciplinary nexus of archival research, applied history, and social science. The studentship can be taken up either full or part-time. Students should have an excellent academic record. A master’s degree in a relevant subject (such as History or War Studies) is a requirement. About the Leverhulme Centre for Slavery in War Nearly 90% of recent armed conflicts have involved some form of slavery. Yet the relationships between slavery and war are little examined and poorly understood, leaving governments, international institutions, and humanitarian actors ill-prepared to prevent, respond, or address deep, long-lasting impacts. In a world facing proliferating conflicts, the Leverhulme Centre for Research on Slavery in War (LCRSW) is the first overarching and integrative academic initiative dedicated to understanding the complex, pervasive, and persistent slavery-war nexus as it has evolved over the centuries. This dual-site research centre (led by the Department of War Studies at King’s College London and the Rights Lab at the University of Nottingham) has been established to shape a new interdisciplinary field of study and a step-change towards the global goal of eliminating forced labour, modern slavery, and human trafficking. The Centre’s research agenda is structured around four interconnected Research Strands (RS): (Re)conceptualising (RS1), Understanding (RS2), Forecasting (RS3), and Tackling (RS4) slavery in war. Doctoral research projects will be embedded within and across these research strands and their teams, working both individually and as a cohort. Together, they will break down disciplinary silos, integrating methodologies from across the AHRC subject remit—primarily history, literature, law, digital humanities, human geography, philosophy, classics, gender studies, political science, and international studies—with cutting-edge data science techniques, including Earth Observation (EO) data analysis, machine learning, large-scale collation and analysis of survivor narratives, geospatial analysis, future-crafting approaches, and novel simulations known as ‘peace- gaming’. Students will also have opportunities to collaborate with our institutions’ partners around the world, across the policy, practitioner and academic sectors. Details of award The award pays UKRI Home Tuition Fees (£5,238 for 2026/27) for PhD students. The award pays full maintenance for all students both home and international. The UKRI Doctoral Stipend for 2026/2027 is £21,805, plus a London Weighting of £2,000/year, plus Collaborative Activity funding at a rate of £600/year. Further details can be found on the UKRI website: www.ukri.org/manage-your award/studentship-guidance/support-for-ukri-funded-students The student is eligible to receive an additional Research Training Support Grant (RTSG) during the course of the project. The project can be undertaken on a full-time or part-time basis. Eligibility This studentship is open to both Home and International applicants. However, the CRSW is limited to one Overseas studentship across the opportunities currently advertised. To be classed as a home student, candidates must meet the following criteria: We are committed to welcoming applications from students from all backgrounds. We particularly welcome applications from Black, Asian, minority ethnic (BAME) backgrounds as they are currently underrepresented at this level in this discipline. We require an upper-second class (2:1) honours degree and a Master’s degree at high merit or above in a discipline directly relevant to the PhD (or international equivalent). Please see here for the English-language requirements for PhD students in the Department of War Studies (Band B): Postgraduate English language entry requirements | King's College London Assessment of applicants Applicants will be assessed by how well they meet the person specification for this position. This may include: An educational and research background that matches this research project. The potential to work effectively and inclusively with a diverse team of people The potential to take initiative and manage a dynamic and complex workload. The potential to develop expertise in new areas related to this subject. A demonstrated interest in and understanding of the proposed area of research, including knowledge of current challenges and opportunities. The potential to undertake continuous personal and professional development. The potential to communicate ideas and findings, verbally and in writing, clearly and effectively. An understanding of relevant research methods. A successful proposal will contain a clearly identified, novel research question, positioned in the context of current historiography. It will also identify relevant sources. Compelling proposals will offer insight into how the candidate may use those sources. How to apply If you have questions about the project or the application process, please contact Kelsey Carthew at crsw@kcl.ac.uk Applicants should apply at the link below and submit the following no later than 5pm on 1 st September 2026: qualtrics.kcl.ac.uk/jfe/form/SV_0UQML35ytEOvOHc Curriculum vitae A personal statement outlining your reasons for pursuing doctoral research at King’s College London A research proposal (5-10 pages in length) that explains your proposed area of focus; primary research question; importance and originality of your topic; initial thoughts on methods and potential case studies; and your familiarity with the existing literature and research on this topic. A sample of academic writing. If you are a current MA student awaiting results of your dissertation, please upload your submitted dissertation as your writing sample. Transcripts of undergraduate and master’s qualifications One academic reference Please submit all materials in English. Use of AI: While we recognise that AI tools can be useful for certain tasks, your application should reflect your own thinking, research interests, skills, and experience rather than AI generated content. Applications that rely heavily on AI-generated content may not demonstrate the originality, critical thinking, and personal insight expected for doctoral study. Please note it is the responsibility of applicants to request references from their referees and ensure that they have been received by this deadline. All documents should be submitted in either MS Word or PDF format. Interviews will be held in September with offers expected by the end of the month . Following the interview, the successful candidate will also need to formally apply to King’s College London and satisfy its admission requirements.

item.title: Research Officer (Comparative Politics)
item.description: Location: Queen Elizabeth House, 3 Mansfield Road, Oxford OX1 3TB The Oxford Department of International Development (ODID) is seeking to recruit a Research Officer. Reporting to Professor Masooda Bano, the post-holder will join a research team funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Advanced Grant, Choosing Islamic Conservatism: Muslim Youth in Europe and the UK and the Question of Social Cohesion. Building on the earlier phases of the project, the team is now establishing the European Muslim Observatory: Comparative Research Infrastructure on Muslim Institutional Development in Europe. The Observatory aims to develop the first systematic comparative research infrastructure documenting the institutional development of Islam and Muslim communities across Europe. It will bring together legal, political, institutional and religious data to examine how Muslim institutions evolve in interaction with constitutional frameworks, state institutions and wider society, creating a lasting research resource for comparative scholarship on Islam in Europe. The Observatory aims to establish a lasting comparative database that will support future academic research, policy engagement and international collaboration beyond the lifetime of the current ERC grant. Successful applicants will become part of the founding research team responsible for designing, developing and implementing this new research infrastructure. This post is offered full-time for 18 months. The successful candidate will have a Master's degree (or equivalent) in Comparative Politics, Political Science, European Studies or a closely related discipline. They will also possess excellent analytical and organisational skills. The ability to work systematically with large volumes of information is essential to this role. At ODID we embrace and cherish our differences, and endeavour to be considerate and welcoming of all. You are most welcome at ODID, without the need to hide any part of who you are. We acknowledge societal inequalities and how these affect us, and those around us, personally and professionally. We hold an Athena Swan bronze award in recognition of our efforts to introduce organisational and cultural changes which promote equality, cherish diversity and create a better working environment for all. We are also taking active steps to promote race equality and reduce the risk of bias and discrimination. We work together to enrich, fortify and grow our community and dedicate our combined efforts to teaching and research to increase our impact and influence in development debates at the national and global level. We encourage all eligible candidates to apply for our vacancies and join us in pursuing our goals. Applications for this vacancy are to be made online. You will be required to upload a CV and supporting statement as part of your online application. Please note that only the CV and supporting statement will be considered; any other documents uploaded will not be reviewed as part of the shortlisting process. Only applications received before 12 midday on Friday, 11 September 2026 can be considered. Contact Person: HR Team Pay Scale: RESEARCH GRADE 6 Contact Email : recruitment@qeh.ox.ac.uk

item.title: PhD Student with Strong Computational Profile for the Project Navigating Negativity: What is a Healthy News Diet?
item.description: The Centre for Journalism, Department of Political Science and Public Management , University of Southern Denmark, Odense, invites applications with a strong computational profile for a three-year full-time PhD scholarship in the project Navigating Negativity: What is a Healthy News Diet? (HEALTHY NEWS), with employment starting from 1 November 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter. The place of employment will be in Odense. The research project—funded by the Velux Foundation—examines when exposure to negative news informs people about important societal issues and when it negatively affects mental well-being and leads to news avoidance. The overall aim is to identify barriers and opportunities for healthy news diets and to assess how the benefits and drawbacks of negative news can be balanced in today’s individualized media environment. Motivated applications are invited from candidates holding a master’s degree in relevant fields, such as computational social science, computer science, communication, political science, or journalism/media studies. The PhD student will be involved in all aspects of the research, from conception, execution, analysis, publishing to public dissemination. The ideal candidate therefore has a high academic level and a good grasp of research designs and methods. Strong computational skills are necessary. The application deadline is 15 September 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST) For more information, please click on the ' Apply ' button above.

item.description: About the role The Conservative Party controls over 60 local authorities and has around 3,500 Councillors across England. Our job is to advocate and be the national voice for our Conservative Councillors, often working with our partners in the Conservative Party, CCHQ, the Shadow MHCLG frontbench team and the voluntary party to ensure the priorities of the Conservative local government team are understood. In addition to this, the LGA Conservative Group is responsible for ensuring the priorities of the Conservative local government team are reflected in the operation of the LGA whether that be through our member led Policy Committees or through our sector led improvement offer. As the Conservative Group Political Officer, you will be responsible for the following: *Supporting Conservative Group members on our Policy Committees with research and briefings. *Working to build our relationships with Conservative leaning think tanks. *Lead on policy work including, bringing together best practice across our Conservative Councils and establishing the principles of what a future Local Government Act could look like for the next Conservative Government. *Drafting articles and briefing the press under the direction of the Head of the Conservative Group Office. *Other responsible duties discharged by the Head of the Conservative Group Office. About you In the fast paced, ever-changing world of local government, we are looking for someone who has a flexible approach and someone who is able to work independently and within a small team. item.title: Personal Operations Assistant
item.description: The Conservative Party is seeking to appoint an exceptional Personal Operations Assistant to the Leader of the Official Opposition. This is an exciting opportunity to join a busy office supporting a senior political figure. As a Personal Ops Assistant, you'll provide day-to-day assistance and organisational support, helping to ensure everything runs smoothly behind the scenes. The role offers a varied workload, from managing tasks and correspondence to assisting at events and supporting day-to-day priorities. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys being organised, proactive, and focused on delivering high-quality support with discretion and professionalism. This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the beginning of their career who is enthusiastic, reliable, and eager to build experience in a fast-paced and rewarding environment. To view the full job description and apply, please visit: https://isw.changeworknow.co.uk/cchq/vms/e/careers/positions/dc0awuqYniI65c9FeOJcHM Closing Date : 21 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews to be held from week commencing 31st August 2026 Application Details https://isw.changeworknow.co.uk/cchq/vms/e/careers/positions/dc0awuqYniI65c9FeOJcHM Website : http://conservatives.com
item.dc:creator: The Conservative Party

item.title: Organiser
item.description: Compass is a growing organisation, with a network of local groups, and is looking for someone to help get these groups election-ready while strengthening our relationships across the progressive political landscape. This is a fantastic time to be working with a dynamic, progressive political organisation with big ambitions. The Organiser will be responsible for powering Compass’ local groups, with a key focus on building our local groups ahead of the next election, and developing relationships across progressive political parties. They will play a key role in helping Compass strengthen its organising infrastructure while building productive relationships with partners outside Labour, including Liberal Democrats, Greens, and Welsh and Scottish nationalists, and with regional leaders working outside Westminster. They will support work across the full range of Compass’ campaigns work, building powerful coalitions in key seats, growing the local groups infrastructure, developing cross-party relationships, and working on cutting through to key constituencies. The role requires someone to use their excellent relationship building skills to work with diverse groups of people to build and grow teams around a shared vision and strategy. The Organiser will work closely with Compass’ Deputy Director, as well as with the Executive Director, Campaigns Officer, Fundraising and Membership Manager, and Media and Press Officer, and alongside a broad network of partners, allies, associates and volunteers. We are looking for someone who is enthusiastic, relational, organised, committed and keen to learn. They should be comfortable working in a small, lively team and with groups and political traditions with different perspectives. Closing Date : 31 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates The application deadline is 5pm. Initial interviews will be held on 4th September, and remaining interviews will be held in early September. We may close applications sooner if suitable candidates are found to advance to the next stage, so early applications are strongly advised. Application Details To find out more and apply for this role, please visit the following page: https://www.compassonline.org.uk/were-hiring-apply-to-be-an-organiser-at-compass/ . Applicants will be asked to upload a 1-page cover letter, a CV, and to answer two questions related to the position. After initial applications close, applicants will be informed if they will be advanced to an interview or not. You can email Compass’ Political Affairs & Organising Officer, Luke, at luke@compassonline.org.uk Website : https://www.compassonline.org.uk/

item.title: Senior Public Affairs Advisor
item.description: The Dad Shift is a non-profit campaign working to champion the cause of active fatherhood - principally through our flagship campaign to improve the UKs statutory paternity leave. We are seeking a highly experienced and well networked senior public affairs consultant to work a day a week alongside our small but extremely senior and award winning team as the government's parental leave review concludes over the next six months. Closing Date : 21 August 2026 Interview/Start Dates Interviews on a rolling basis, to start asap. Application Details Email George@dadshift.org.uk with a CV and a couple of paragraphs on a) why you would be the right person to help persuade this Labour government to improve statutory paternity leave in the next 9 months, and b) what you think the principal argument our campaign needs to make to get this over the line. Website : http://www.dadshift.org.uk
